statement: For every integer i with 0 <= i < n-1, define P(i) = sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k] and S(i) = sum_{k=i+1}^{n-1} nums[k]. Let V = { i | 0 <= i < n-1 and P(i) >= S(i) }. The function returns a result r and r equals the number of elements of V, i.e. r is exactly the number of valid splits in nums.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000. All sums below are ordinary integer sums of the i64 values.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, ways_to_split_array(nums) returns a result; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and 0 <= r <= n-1.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: Let T = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} nums[k]. The function returns a result r and r = |{ i | 0 <= i < n-1 and 2 * (sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k]) >= T }|.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: Let W = { i | 0 <= i < n-1 and sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k] < sum_{k=i+1}^{n-1} nums[k] }. The function returns a result r and r = (n-1) - |W|.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = n-1 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k] >= sum_{k=i+1}^{n-1} nums[k].
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k] < sum_{k=i+1}^{n-1} nums[k].
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r > 0 if and only if there exists an integer i with 0 <= i < n-1 such that sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k] >= sum_{k=i+1}^{n-1} nums[k].
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and, if nums[k] >= 0 for every k with 0 <= k < n, then there exists an integer t with 0 <= t <= n-1 such that: for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, the split i is valid, meaning sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k] >= sum_{k=i+1}^{n-1} nums[k], if and only if i >= t; and r = n-1-t.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and, if nums[k] <= 0 for every k with 0 <= k < n, then there exists an integer t with -1 <= t <= n-2 such that: for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, the split i is valid, meaning sum_{k=0}^{i} nums[k] >= sum_{k=i+1}^{n-1} nums[k], if and only if i <= t; and r = t+1.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and, for every positive integer c such that -100000 <= c * nums[k] <= 100000 for every k with 0 <= k < n, the call ways_to_split_array(nums_c) on the array nums_c[k] = c * nums[k] also returns a result and that result equals r.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.

statement: If there is an integer c such that nums[k] = c for every k with 0 <= k < n, then the function returns a result r and: if c > 0 then r = (n-1) - ceil_half; if c = 0 then r = n-1; if c < 0 then r = floor_half + 1, where ceil_half is the least integer q with 2q >= n-2 and floor_half is the greatest integer q with 2q <= n-2.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 2 <= n <= 100000; for every k with 0 <= k < n, -100000 <= nums[k] <= 100000.
